Take the relation taught for 'The Three Economic Sectors' and work with: primary = 45, secondary = 4, tertiary = 80. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of sectors.
Explain in your own words what 'The Three Economic Sectors' refers to.
questions.a: Economic activities are grouped into three sectors by what they do: the primary sector draws goods from nature, the secondary sector makes products, and the tertiary sector provides services that support both.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The Three Economic Sectors'.
questions.a: Classification brings order: grouping thousands of activities into three sectors shows how the economy fits together.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'The Three Economic Sectors', in plain ASCII form.

concepts.title: The Primary Sector: Gifts of Nature

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'The Primary Sector: Gifts of Nature' refers to.
questions.a: The primary sector takes what nature offers: farming, livestock rearing, fishing, forestry and mining, the first step of every product we later buy in a shop.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The Primary Sector: Gifts of Nature'.
questions.a: Every economy begins in the field, the forest, the sea and the mine: nature gives the first goods.

questions.q: Under which section is 'The Primary Sector: Gifts of Nature' taught, and from which source text?
Explain in your own words what 'Secondary and Tertiary Sectors' refers to.
questions.a: The secondary sector turns raw materials into products in factories, from pharmaceutical plants to furniture units; the tertiary sector provides services such as banking, teaching, transport, software and restaurants that support the other two.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Secondary and Tertiary Sectors'.
questions.a: Making and serving: the secondary sector builds goods, the tertiary sector moves, sells and supports them.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Secondary and Tertiary Sectors' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Secondary and tertiary sectors (source: fees114.txt, Secondary and tertiary sectors)

concepts.title: How the Sectors Depend on Each Other

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'How the Sectors Depend on Each Other' refers to.
questions.a: The sectors form a chain: farms grow cotton, mills weave cloth, shops and transport sell and move it; each sector buys from and sells to the others, so growth in one lifts all.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'How the Sectors Depend on Each Other'.
questions.a: No sector stands alone: the shirt on your back is a relay race from field to factory to shop.

questions.q: Under which section is 'How the Sectors Depend on Each Other' taught, and from which source text?
